The three core primitives—betting line overreaction, coach decision bias, and stale line inference—are rooted in behavioral and temporal inefficiencies in NFL markets. Overreaction implies that betting lines respond excessively to new information, creating negative autocorrelation in line movements. This is modeled as a stochastic process where current line deviations inversely correlate with prior ones. Coach bias reflects systematic underestimation of success probabilities, particularly in 4th-down scenarios, which creates exploitable inefficiencies. Stale line inference arises from delayed adjustments in sportsbooks, where scraping pre-adjustment lines yields outdated values. These primitives form a dual framework: one temporal (overreaction, stale lines) and one behavioral (coach bias). Each has a distinct failure mode—overreaction leads to mispricing, bias to incorrect expectations, and stale lines to arbitrage opportunities. The interplay of these primitives enables both GSI’s Bayesian inference and GSE’s situational reasoning to identify inefficiencies.
